author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This function replaces every bracketed key in a string with its value from a lookup table. It first turns the `knowledge` array of `[key, value]` pairs into a `Map` for fast lookups, then scans the string `s` one character at a time. When it sees an opening `(`, it flips a **reading** flag on and resets a `temp` buffer that will collect the key's characters. When it sees a closing `)`, it flips the flag off and appends the value found for `temp` in the map, or a `?` if the key is unknown (that's what `map.get(temp) ?? '?'` does). Any other character is either added to `temp` while reading a key, or appended directly to the result `res` when outside brackets. The built-up `res` string is returned at the end.

author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This is a compact version of the same idea: swap every `(key)` in the string for its value from `knowledge`. It builds a `Map` from the `[key, value]` pairs, then splits `s` on every `(` or `)` using the regex `/\(|\)/`. Because the brackets always come in matched pairs, the resulting pieces **alternate** between plain text and bracketed keys, so every odd-indexed piece is a key. The `map` callback uses `i & 1` (a bitwise check for odd indices) to spot those key pieces and replace them with `map.get(x) ?? '?'`, which returns the stored value or a `?` if the key isn't known, while even-indexed pieces are kept as-is. Finally `join('')` glues the pieces back into a single string.
